newsitem.title: CHINA: Beijing-Kowloon line trains to speed up in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Beijing-Kowloon line trains to speed up in 1997.

text.p: Trains on the line that will eventually link China's capital Beijing with Hong Kong will run faster in the run-up to the British colony reverting to Chinese rule next year.

Trains on the Beijing-Kowloon line, which for now could go as far as the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen that borders Hong Kong, would run at 100 km/hr (62 miles/hr) from April 1, 1997, an official of the Railway Ministry said on Wednesday.
This would be 40 km/hr (25 miles/hr) faster than the current speed and cut the north-south journey time to 36 hours from 48 hours, the official told Reuters by telephone.
The line opened in September, but would complete its final leg to Hong Kong only after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997.
China would add more freight trains to the current 10 next year to cope with demands but had not decided on how many, the official said.
The Beijing-Kowloon railway runs for 2,356 km (1,464 miles) and cost 40 billion yuan ($4.8 billion) to build.
